one_line_contribution: With retrieved content, cached prefix and message format held fixed, the proposal defines and measures a 'harm mass' (test-retest-corrected paired-table probability that retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt solves) and argues/tests that it upper-bounds what any retrieval-timing policy can gain over always-retrieve, on ALFWorld at a natural and a hand-planted mislabelled-twin bank, with side experiments on whether the query at stall matters and whether a cached recovery rulebook substitutes for stall retrieval.
closest_prior_work: Verified: arXiv:2607.24010, 'When Should Active RAG Retrieve? A Budget-Aware Evaluation of Utility, Calibration, and Cost' (2026-07-27, verified via s2cli.py paper on channel (a); S2 abstract: 'recasting active retrieval as utility estimation, where retrieval is valuable only through its marginal correctness change over a no-retrieval answer'). That is the same accounting one level up: the harm mass is exactly the negative half of that marginal-correctness decomposition, and the budget-aware operating-point framing already makes the 'timing moves you along a cost curve, not above it' point. What survives as new here is the instantiation (trajectories not QA documents, a paired-seed estimator with a test-retest term subtracted, prefix-caching token cost) and the deliberate manipulation of the harm level with a twin bank — real but incremental. Two further verified threats: arXiv:2604.20572 (ProactAgent, 'Ask Only When Needed', 2026-04-22, cit 4, verified) already learns when and what to retrieve from an experience base for lifelong agents, i.e. the policy class this proposal claims to bound but never trains; and arXiv:2607.20972 ('Delivery, Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory as a Harness Property for Coding Agents', 2026-07-23, verified) stakes the opposite headline — that delivery/timing is the harness property and cue-anchored injection beats voluntary reads — so the proposal's contribution is largely to contradict a claim someone else already published, on one environment, in a hand-built harm regime. On the estimator side, arXiv:2404.10198 (RAG vs internal prior tug-of-war, verified via search) and arXiv:2608.22856 (repeat-aware audit of answer churn, which likewise nets flips against repeat noise) show that both the 'retrieval breaks what the model already solves' phenomenon and the repeat-corrected flip accounting are established; the assembly, not the parts, is what is new.
strongest_objection: The headline bound is close to definitional, and the plan's own text says so. The proposal states that late-read-only mass is the only channel that can breach the bound, which makes P6's upper falsifier (G > Delta_harm + 8) and its second falsifier (Lambda >= 8) the same event: P6 is not an independent test of an inequality, it is a padded restatement of the estimand it is compared against, with the pad equal to the noise floor. Worse, every threshold in P1-P6 is set at exactly the pre-registered +/-8 floor, so the equivalence clauses (P2a/b/c, P4 curated-vs-planted, P5 cell12-vs-cell8) can be 'passed' by a null result that the design has no power to distinguish from a real effect — there is no undecided band between floor and margin, which is the standard TOST requirement. The dilution is the third blow: the stall fires on at most 50% of episodes and P3's random key hits the right planted item on 20% of firings by construction, so an 8-net whole-sample gap needs a ~16-20 point within-row effect at unchanged noise. Finally the generality claim overreaches what is run: the abstract bounds 'any retrieval-timing policy (start, fixed schedule, on stall, learned)' but no learned policy is trained and the two triggers are hand-written, on one environment, one reader, one k=3 goal-keyed block; and the regime where the bound actually binds is a 1:1 mislabelled-twin bank the authors built, which no deployment resembles. A reviewer will read the result as 'a tautology confirmed in a synthetic harm regime, and an equivalence declared at the noise floor everywhere else.'
what_would_fix_it: (1) Decouple margins from the floor: add seeds/games until the paired floor is about +/-4, then set equivalence margins strictly inside it and difference thresholds at 1.5-2x it, so a null and a miss are separable outcomes. (2) Stop testing the bound as a point comparison with a full-floor pad — report a cluster-bootstrap CI on the difference G - Delta_harm(distractor) directly, and give Lambda its own CI on the doubly-failing subset with a falsifier above that subset's scaled floor (on ~25% of rows the scaled floor is near +/-16 against a threshold of 8). (3) Define firing rows once, from a single pre-read static3_B trigger log applied identically to both arms, and score every stall contrast (P2b, P3, P5's cell13-cell12) on that subset with a subset-scaled floor, since the whole-sample scoring throws away half the signal and keeps all the noise. (4) Realize the ceiling as an arm rather than asserting it: train one actual timing policy on pre-read features and run a cheap per-type retrieve/skip gate, and show that both land inside the bound — that converts 'no policy with the same content can exceed the harm mass' from a claim about a policy class into evidence about it. (5) Add one unengineered harm level (e.g. a self-generated bank with measured, not planted, mislabelling) beside the 1:1 twins, and log twin retrieval rate as an outcome-independent manipulation check, so P1's distractor clause is not a re-description of bank construction. With (1)-(4) this becomes a defensible, if narrow, negative result; without them the design cannot lose.
missing_baseline: A realized timing policy, and a timing control matched on rows. The plan's only ceiling is the cross-fitted oracle, explicitly descriptive with no cell, so nothing in the experiment ever exercises the policy class the headline bounds: a reviewer will demand (a) a trained retrieve/skip decision head on pre-read features, and (b) the cheap per-type gate that Measurement A already motivates (clean/heat/cool +26.7/+25.6/+19.6 vs look-at +4.8 with CI including 0 — skipping retrieval on look-at is a budget policy that should cost nothing in success and save tokens), which directly probes whether the value lives in timing or in selection. Also missing: a yoked random-step read, delivered at a step drawn from cell 4's own firing-step distribution on the same rows. Cell 6's fixed step-10 schedule is not row-matched to the trigger, so the design has a random-key control for the query (cell 9) but no random-time control for the time, which is the very variable under test.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this pipeline — it names the channel, gives four query classes with IDs, and its two load-bearing IDs check out: I verified arXiv:2607.24010 (title and abstract match, cit 1) and arXiv:2604.20572 (ProactAgent, 2026-04-22, cit 4) with s2cli.py paper on channel (a), plus arXiv:2607.20972 (Delivery, Not Storage), arXiv:2505.00234 (NeurIPS 2025), arXiv:2607.07380, arXiv:2510.16724 (dated 2025-10, not 2026 as the digest ordering implies), arXiv:2305.06983 (FLARE), arXiv:2403.14403 (Adaptive-RAG), arXiv:2303.11366 (Reflexion). Could not verify: the bare Semantic Scholar hash s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (no arXiv id supplied), and the collision-check-only ids 2608.25625, 2605.30712, 2606.27136, 2603.24639, 2604.01664, 2604.13717 (not needed for the novelty argument, so not chased). My own queries, all answered by channel (a) — the s2cli command (S2 + HF); WebSearch was unavailable and WebFetch is blocked, so neither was used: (i) 'when to retrieve timing policy upper bound value of retrieval agent memory always retrieve' --recent -> 12 hits, nearest arXiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap), 2603.04549 (adaptive memory admission control), 2606.05684 (AdaMEM); none bounds the timing decision. (ii) 'retrieval hurts episodes solved without retrieval harm upper bound adaptive retrieval headroom' -> effectively empty on the mechanism; nearest arXiv:2501.04899 (SUGAR, confidence-gated retrieval). (iii) 'failure triggered retrieval at stall embodied agent ALFWorld inject exemplar mid episode versus at start' --recent -> arXiv:2607.08716 (Remember When It Matters: proactive memory for long-horizon agents), arXiv:2607.13884 (Experience Memory Graph: one-shot error correction from failed and expert trajectories — closest to the planted-recovery bank and NOT cited by the proposal), arXiv:2608.11772 (Diagnosis Before Recovery: selective self-correction 'without uniformly expanding context'), arXiv:2607.10608; none reports a harm-mass bound. (iv) 'ProactAgent ask only when needed proactive retrieval from memory and skills' -> confirmed arXiv:2604.20572. (v) 'oracle upper bound on routing decision skyline how much can a perfect when-to-retrieve policy gain' --recent -> EMPTY on topic (returned VLSI routing, bilevel optimization, transit design); reported as empty, not as novelty. (vi) 'retrieval degrades answers the model already gets right, flips correct to incorrect' -> arXiv:2404.10198 (tug-of-war between RAG and internal prior) and arXiv:2608.22856 (repeat-aware audit of corpus-induced answer churn — repeat-noise-corrected flip accounting, the closest methodological analogue to Delta_harm and also uncited). (vii) 'in-context demonstration delivery timing, prefix caching accuracy-cost frontier' --recent -> arXiv:2607.12161 (Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction: success-adjusted billed cost, caching dominates expense — relevant to the cost axis and uncited), 2606.17016 (TokenPilot), 2604.05404 (PTE). (viii) 'planted mislabelled distractor items in experience bank, controlled corruption, harm to agent success' --recent -> nothing on point; nearest arXiv:2605.10828 (nonlinear impact of misleading information in long context). Verdict on the check itself: honest and reasonably searched, but it under-weighs the two threats it itself surfaces — 2607.24010 already prices retrieval as marginal correctness over no-retrieval under a budget, and 2607.20972 already asserts the opposite delivery claim — and it never searched the 'retrieval flips what the model already gets right' home literature, where the phenomenon and the repeat-corrected flip estimator both predate this proposal. Novelty is scored on that: new packaging of an established accounting, not a new claim.
